Traits Eidolon, Stand · Size Small or Tiny · Suggested Attacks ram (bludgeoning), bite (piercing)

Stand Attributes Con +3, Int –2, Wis +1, Cha +1 · Skills Athletics, Stealth · Senses program sense (imprecise, 60 feet, for the one stimulus its program tracks) · Speed 25 feet

Grades Durability must be A or B. Precision must be D.

Examples Sheer Heart Attack, Black Sabbath, Notorious B.I.G

You set the stand loose on a program and let it hunt while you do other things. It acts even on turns you don't Act Together, Mark points it at the enemy that matters, Feed the Program trades one of your actions for a second stand action, Set Program (6) sends it beyond your range without sharing damage, Relentless Program and Undying Program make it hard to stop out of your sight, and a Set Program stand turns Autonomous: nearly impossible to beat head-on, so enemies have to starve its program or come for you. Its Precision is low and it attacks allies who match the program, so choosing the program and keeping allies clear is the skill. Class feats like Stand Cry and Stand Guard keep you useful while it works. Pick this if you want a relentless hunter that keeps up pressure without your attention, and you're happy to manage the risk to your allies.

Initial (1st)—Program When you Manifest the stand, give it one program: heat, movement, the creature that last damaged you, or a marked creature. You gain the Mark and Feed the Program actions. On a turn you don't Act Together, the stand still spends 1 action at the end of your turn to Stride toward or Strike the nearest creature that matches, allies included. To call it off: if no creature matching the program is within the stand's senses, spend 1 action (concentrate) on your turn to end or swap the program. Otherwise it takes 2 actions (concentrate) to force it to stop. The stand stays manifested either way. Once the end-of-turn action starts it can't be stopped, so plan before you end your turn. The Set Program feat is stricter: that stand can't be recalled until no matching target remains, except by spending 3 actions to force it to stop.

7th—Relentless Program Out of your sight, the stand stops sharing damage with you: it has its own Hit Points equal to 5 × your level (damage to it doesn't reach you) and gains +2 to saves. Autonomous: while it runs a Set Program (the Set Program feat), it also gains resistance to all damage equal to twice your level (half that against force, spirit and ghost touch), immunity to mental, fear and death effects and to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{grabbed}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{restrained}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{paralyzed}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{slowed} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{stunned}, +3 to hit, Strikes that roll damage dice equal to your level (minimum 8), and it never retreats. When an Autonomous stand is destroyed, it reforms at the start of its own next turn with half its Hit Points. While you're out of its sight you can't Act Together with it, but Feed the Program still works from any distance (your action gives it a second action that turn). Starving the program: if no creature matching its program is within its 60-foot program sense at the start of its turn, it is dormant and does nothing that turn; after 2 dormant turns in a row it unmanifests. The user: if you are knocked out, killed or forced to call it off, it loses these benefits and unmanifests.

13th—Undying Program When your stand is destroyed while out of your sight, it reforms at the start of your next turn with full Hit Points, even if you are out of its range. An Autonomous stand (Set Program) reforms at the start of its own next turn with full Hit Points, every time: only starving the program or dealing with you ends it.
